lead43_altitude_4q_split_half_alternatin.classification_evidence: Whole interval below zero on this specific alternating-game-halves construction (reproduces CX15's -0.6056 on the 2013-2025 window). NOT recorded refuted_mechanism: this measures season-to-season ORDERING of a noisy per-season mean (n=8-9 games per half), a different estimand from the fixed Denver-vs-league Q4 contrast, which stays positive and mostly excludes zero on every other cut in this experiment (sections 1-2 of docs/altitude_fourth_quarter.md); both season-halves' own means are themselves mostly positive (14 of 16 season-half values positive), so this is noisy re-ordering, not a sign flip of the underlying quantity. no_split_half_reliability is not invoked as a closing ground for that reason.
lead43_altitude_4q_split_half_alternatin.description: Split-half reliability of Denver's season-level Q4-share scoring trait: alternating-game halves within season, correlated across seasons, 2009-2025 (CX15 method extended)
lead43_altitude_4q_split_half_alternatin.notes: scripts/altitude_fourth_quarter_screen.py section 4 (alternating_games_scoring_2009_2025); matches CX15's exact split-half method (docs/coaching_leads.md), extended from 13 to 17 seasons.
lead43_altitude_4q_split_half_alternatin.plain_summary: One specific way of splitting Denver's seasons in half finds no consistent year-to-year pattern, but the underlying fourth-quarter home advantage itself stays positive in both halves -- this checks a different, noisier question than whether the advantage is real.
